transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately that brought you here?

Well, I guess... what brings me here is that my talking gets all mixed up lately. I try to explain things to people, like about the keys at work, and then... then it goes to the jail, and the prayer rug, and then chess pieces. People just tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. It's like the words just come out all jumbled.
Have you been experiencing any unusual or strange thoughts lately that others might not understand or believe?

Well, yeah, I have. People definitely don't believe me about what's happening at work. 

I know the people in the building have marked me. They use the hallway lights and give each other these little looks just to warn each other about me when I'm cleaning. My supervisor tried to tell me it wasn't happening... he even pulled up the security camera and showed me there was nothing on it. But I still feel sure they're doing it. I know what I'm seeing, even if they don't get it.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so others can hear them?

No... no, I haven't had anything like that. My thoughts are my own. Nobody's putting them there or taking them away, and I don't hear them out loud or anything. It's just the stuff happening around me that I notice, not people messing with my head like that.
Have you noticed yourself moving differently, like being slower than usual, repeating movements, or having trouble doing things that require coordination?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm moving around the same as always when I'm working, sweeping and mopping and all that. I'm not slow, and I don't get stuck doing the same thing over and over. My coordination is fine, I can still do my job just fine. It's just the people watching me that's the problem, not how I'm moving.
Do you feel that certain people or groups are specifically targeting you or trying to harm you in some way?

Yeah, like I was saying earlier... that's exactly what it is. The people in the building have marked me. They're targeting me. Even after my supervisor sat me down and showed me there was nothing on the security camera, I still feel sure they're doing it. I know they use the hallway lights and give each other those little looks just to warn each other about me. So, yeah, I definitely feel like I'm being targeted by them.
Have you ever found yourself acting in a strange or disorganized way, like not responding to others, moving very slowly, or doing things that don't make sense to you afterward?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm not moving slow or acting strange. Like I said, I'm just doing my job, cleaning up, going about my day. I don't get confused about what I'm doing or just stop talking to people. I just do my work and try to keep an eye on what they're doing to me. But my own actions? No, they make sense to me.
Have you ever felt like your actions were being controlled by an outside force, or that you were being made to do things against your will by something or someone else?

No, I haven't felt anything like that. Nobody is... taking over my body or making me do things. I'm the one in control of myself. I mean, they're definitely watching me and trying to mess with my head, but they can't physically force me to do something against my will. When I'm working or just doing whatever, it's just me deciding to do it.
Can you tell me more about what you mean when you say the people in the building have 'marked you'? Have you noticed any physical signs or specific actions that make you feel this way?

Well, it's just... I know it sounds crazy to other people, but I know what I see. When I say they marked me, I mean they've decided I'm the one they need to watch. Like I told my supervisor, I know they're doing it. He sat me down, right? He played the security tape back for me and said, "Look, there's nobody doing anything, no one is messing with you." But... I still know they are. 

It's the lights. When I walk down the hall to empty the bins, the lights flicker in this specific way. It's a signal. And the people who work in the offices, when they pass each other, they give these little looks. Just a quick glance, but I know it's about me. It's them warning each other that I'm coming. The camera might not catch it, or maybe they know where the blind spots are, but I'm absolutely sure it's happening.
Do you feel that things people do around you – like their actions, gestures, or even things on TV or the radio – have a special meaning for you that others don't understand?

Yeah, that's exactly what I was just talking about. Like I was saying, even when my supervisor sat me down and showed me the security tape, and he pointed out that there was nothing on the camera... I still felt absolutely sure that the people in the building had marked me. 

Other people just don't understand it. My boss didn't get it at all. They just see a normal hallway or people walking by, but I know they're using those flickering lights and those little looks to warn each other about me. So, yeah, those actions definitely have a meaning to me that nobody else seems to get.
Do you feel that things people do around you — like their actions, gestures, or even things on TV or the radio — have a special meaning for you that others don't understand?

Well, like I was just saying... yeah, I do. Even after my supervisor sat me down and played back the security tape to prove there was nothing there, it didn't change anything for me. I still know they've marked me. 

Other people might just see a flickering light in the hallway or two people giving each other a quick look, but I know what it really means. It's them warning each other about me. So, yes, those things definitely have a special meaning to me, even if nobody else sees it.

Do you feel that events happening around you — like things people say, things you see on TV, or other things in your environment — are directed at you or have a special meaning for you personally, even if others don’t see it that way?

Yeah, I think we're going over the same ground here, doc. Like I just explained, yes, I do feel that way. 

It's just like the situation at work I told you about. My supervisor played that security tape back for me, right? He pointed at the screen and said, "Look, there's nobody doing anything." But I still knew, deep down, that the people in the building had marked me. 

When I see those hallway lights flicker, or when I catch those office workers giving each other those little looks... to me, it's clear as day. They're warning each other about me. Other people don't see it, they just think it's normal stuff, but I know it's directed at me. So, yes, things in my environment definitely have a special meaning for me personally.

Do you feel that everyday events or actions that don’t seem related to you — like things strangers do, things on TV, or random events — have a special meaning for you or are directed at you personally?

Doc, I feel like you keep asking me the exact same thing. Yes, I do. 

Like I keep saying, my supervisor showed me the camera to try and prove nothing was there, but I still felt absolutely sure the people in that building had marked me. When I see the hallway lights flicker or catch them giving each other those little looks, I know they are using all of that to warn each other about me. So yeah, those everyday things are definitely directed at me, even if nobody else gets it.
Do you feel that things that happen around you, like people's actions or things you see or hear, are specifically meant for you, even if they don't seem connected to you at first?

Look, doctor, I don't know how many different ways I can say this. Yes. We've been over this. 

Like I've been telling you... my supervisor showed me that security footage to prove I was wrong. But it didn't matter what the camera showed. I just know, without a doubt, that the people in that building marked me. The flickering lights in the hallway, the way they glance at each other... it's all connected. It's them warning each other about me. So yes, things that happen around me are meant for me.
Do you feel that things people do around you — like their actions, gestures, or even things on TV or the radio — have a special meaning for you that others don't understand?

Doc, are you just reading off a list? Because I swear I've answered this exact same thing like three times already. 

Yes. It's exactly what I just said. My supervisor showed me the camera, showed me there was nothing on the tape, but I still felt completely sure that the people in the building had marked me. The hallway lights flickering, those little looks they give each other... they're using all of that to warn each other about me. So, yeah, it means something to me that other people just don't understand.
